title: Latency Budgeting and Decisive Fallback Canvas
author: Sofia Patel
content:
Overview

This page defines a compact, operator-friendly canvas for latency budgeting across LLM inference stacks and a decisive fallback matrix to keep customer-facing routes within SLOs during transient or sustained degradation. The goal is to give oncall and platform operators a single reference that ties SLO targets, dashboard signals, alerts, immediate mitigation steps, longer-term remediation, and roadmap work into one actionable artifact.

Scope

- Applies to all public and dedicated inference routes (hosted API, dedicated, and private proxies)
- Focuses on network + runtime tail-latency (p95/p99), token emission latency, and request-level end-to-end latency budgets
- Integrates with: metrics backends (Prometheus/OTel), observability dashboards (Grafana), alerting (PagerDuty/Slack), runtime feature flags, and model variant catalog

When to use this canvas

1. During oncall when a latency SLO is burning and the root cause is uncertain.
2. As a runbook fragment for runbooks that span regions or model variants.
3. For product and platform roadmap planning—use the canvas outputs to prioritize capacity, caching, and quantization work.

Decision canvas (at-a-glance)

- Primary SLO: route.successful_requests.latency_p95 < 300ms (example target for low-latency routes).
- Secondary SLOs: p99 < 700ms; token_emission_p95 < 50ms per token.
- Critical thresholds:
  - Warning: p95 > 0.6 * target for 5m
  - Urgent: p95 > target for 2m OR p99 > 1.1 * target for 5m
  - Degraded: sustained p95 above target for > 10m or increased error rate > 0.5%

Interpretation matrix (quick):

- High latency + low error rate: likely resource contention (GPU saturation, kernel stall) or bad batching heuristics -> consider soft-eviction/scale-up, temporary model downgrade, or reduce batch window.
- High latency + high error rate: likely queue/backpressure or upstream failures -> enable circuit-breaker and route to fallback variant.
- Regional-only latency: network / region capacity -> shift traffic to healthy region if cross-region routing available.

Latency budget table (example template)

| Component | Allowed p95 (ms) | Rationale | Owner |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Edge proxy (ingress) | 50 | Connection setup + TLS | eng-platform:edge-team |
| Router / priority queue | 30 | Scheduling and demux | eng-platform:router-team |
| Runtime scheduling & batching | 140 | Queueing + kernel exec | eng-serving-runtime |
| Model token emission | 50 | Token generation per token | research/serving |
| Post-processing & serialization | 30 | JSON + metrics | eng-platform:sidecar |
| Total E2E target | 300 | p95 budget | product-owner |

How to read and adjust budgets

1. Capture production histograms for each component (p50/p95/p99).
2. If a component exceeds its budget, add margin from less-critical components only after cross-checking product impact.
3. Document the budget change in the SLO config and note the justification in the retrospective tracker.

Dashboards and alerts (concrete examples)

Recommended dashboard panels (names assume Grafana):
- Route: latency_slo_panel (p50/p95/p99, request rate, error rate)
- Kernel: kernel_exec_time_by_model (percentile heatmap)
- Queue: request_queue_depth (by tenant & priority)
- Token emitter: token_emit_latency (per model family)
- Fallback health: fallback_success_rate (how often fallbacks return acceptable responses)

Example alert rules (Prometheus-style pseudo YAML)

- name: RouteHighLatencyWarning
  expr: |
    histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(route_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, route)) > 0.6 * 300
  for: 5m
  labels: { severity: warning }
  annotations: { summary: "p95 for {{ $labels.route }} approaching budget" }

- name: RouteHighLatencyUrgent
  expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(route_latency_bucket[2m])) by (le, route)) > 300
  for: 2m
  labels: { severity: page }
  annotations: { runbook: "Runbook:LatencyBudgetRunbook" }

Runbook fragment: LatencyBudgetRunbook (immediate steps)

1. Triage (0–2 minutes):
   - Acknowledge page in PagerDuty and post initial context to #platform-oncall with route, region, and recent deploys.
   - Check the latency_slo_panel for route and model family.
2. Quick mitigations (2–10 minutes):
   - If runtime kernel_exec_time_by_model spikes: toggle JIT-kernel fallback for the model (feature flag: runtime.jit.disable_for_model=<model-id>) and observe 1–2 p95 windows.
   - If queue depth is high: reduce route concurrency limit (api.route.<route>.concurrency) or increase batch window carefully for background tiers.\   - If network/region degradation: enable cross-region failover (traffic-switcher runbook) to target region with >=99.9% prefix-cache health.
3. Decisive fallback (10–30 minutes):
   - If mitigations do not reduce p95 by 30%: enable model-variant fallback policy for the route (route.config.fallback = { strategy: "model_variant", variants: ["small-opt-q4", "llm-fast-8bit"] }).
   - If fallbacks fail or degrade quality unacceptably: apply soft-degradation to non-critical features (reduce response length, disable embeddings-heavy enrichment) and notify product.
4. Stabilize & escalate (30–120 minutes):
   - Open an incident in the incident tracker, assign owners (runtime, router, infra), and set severity.
   - Schedule a degradation postmortem if SLO was breached > 30 minutes or customer-impacting.

Quality guardrail checklist for fallbacks

- Minimum acceptable quality threshold per route (automated): route.quality_eval.score >= 0.85 over canary prompt-set after fallback.
- If quality < threshold: revert fallback and instead apply capacity-based mitigations (scale-up or tenant-level soft-throttling).
- Notify product and customer-success for any fallback that persists > 1 hour.

Telemetry & experiment hooks

- Whenever a fallback is enabled, the platform must record: route_id, original_model_id, fallback_model_id, triggering_alert, operator_id, start_time. This enables retrospective quality and cost analysis.
- Use synthetic-canary harness to validate fallback behavior automatically before auto-rollout.

Retrospective triggers and post-incident actions

Create a lightweight retrospective when any of these are true:
- SLO breach p95/p99 > 1h
- Customer complaint escalation opened
- Fallback used for > 2h or repeatedly within 24h window

Required retrospective outputs (to be tracked in the incident ticket):
- Root cause hypothesis and evidence
- Short-term action (config tweak, rollback, extra capacity) with owner and due date
- Medium-term action (runtime kernel patch, caching strategy, model re-quantization) added to platform roadmap with estimated effort
- Measurement plan: how we'll validate the fix (dashboards, synthetic tests, SLA smoke tests)

Roadmap tie-ins (examples)

- Q2 2025: Deploy kernel-level adaptive batch sizing (reduces average runtime bias and shortens p95 tails) -> priority: high
- Q3 2025: Implement per-route quality canaries to measure fallback regression automatically -> priority: mid
- Q4 2025: Add cross-region pre-warm pools to reduce failover cold-starts -> priority: mid-high

Ownership and contacts

- Oncall rotation: eng-platform oncall (primary) -> @oncall-platform
- Runtime owner: eng-serving-runtime (owners: Marco Alvarez, Lena Kim)
- Router owner: eng-platform/router-team (owner: Malik Thompson)
- Product contact for SLOs: product-observability (owner: Priya Nair)

Examples and case studies (short)

1) Case: Sudden kernel stall (Black Friday simulation)\- Symptom: p95 jumps to 700ms while error rate stays <0.1%\- Immediate action: disable JIT-kernel for affected model; enable spare-preemptible pool; open incident.\- Outcome: p95 recovered to 260ms within 18 minutes; follow-up: kernel microbenchmark and hotfix scheduled.

2) Case: Regional network blip affecting EU region\- Symptom: EU-only p95 elevated; global routes stable\- Immediate action: shift <30% of traffic to US region via traffic-switcher and notify account teams for impacted customers within GDPR allowed routing.

Appendix: useful CLI snippets and alert patch template

- Toggle fallback for a route (CLI):
  redwoodctl routes update --route my-chat-route --set fallback.strategy=model_variant --set fallback.variants=[llm-fast-8bit,small-opt-q4] --operator $USER

- Example alert patch (annotation addition):
  curl -X POST $ALERTMGR/api/v2/alerts -d '{"labels":{"alertname":"RouteHighLatencyUrgent","route":"my-chat-route"},"annotations":{"runbook":"https://confluence/internal/eng-platform/runbooks/latencybudget"}}'

Maintenance notes

- Update this canvas at each SLO recalculation and after every major runtime deploy.
- Keep a changelog entry at the bottom of the SLO config.
